paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates accuracy (ACC) outcomes for six model/editing conditions across different co-occurrence numbers, with all series shown on the same axes and identified by a legend. The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale, with major tick labels at approximately \(10^{1}\), \(10^{2}\), and \(10^{3}\) (the plotted points appear at about 3, 30, 300, and 3000). The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)”, is on a linear scale, and spans roughly from 37% to 67%, with labeled ticks at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, and 65. The Base series is a black solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 38.5% at co-occurrence \(\sim\)3 to about 41.8% at \(\sim\)30, reaching about 44.0% at \(\sim\)300 and remaining near 44.0% at \(\sim\)3000. FT is a blue solid line with downward-pointing triangle markers, rising from about 40.0% (\(\sim\)3) to about 43.3% (\(\sim\)30), then to about 46.1% (\(\sim\)300) and about 47.7% (\(\sim\)3000). IKE is a red solid line with upward-pointing triangle markers, moving from about 43.0% (\(\sim\)3) to about 45.0% (\(\sim\)30), then to about 46.6% (\(\sim\)300) and about 49.4% (\(\sim\)3000). MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, increasing from about 44.5% (\(\sim\)3) to about 48.8% (\(\sim\)30), then to about 54.0% (\(\sim\)300) and about 56.5% (\(\sim\)3000). MEMIT is a purple solid line with hexagon-like markers, rising from about 43.8% (\(\sim\)3) to about 51.2% (\(\sim\)30), then to about 53.0% (\(\sim\)300) and about 54.8% (\(\sim\)3000). ROME is a green solid line with square markers, increasing from about 51.1% (\(\sim\)3) to about 57.2% (\(\sim\)30), then to about 62.3% (\(\sim\)300) and about 66.2% (\(\sim\)3000).
